title: Tuning Charge Density Wave transitions through lattice strain in NbSe3
authors: Antoine Gallo Frantz, Aleksander Sinchenko, Luc Ortega, Pavel Grigoriev, Vladislav Kochev, Pierre Godard, Pierre Olivier Renault, Dominique Thiaudiere, David Le Bolloch, Vincent Jacques
abstract: The Charge Density Wave (CDW) state is a perfect example of a combined structural and electronic state, both characterized by a periodic lattice distortion and an electronic modulation of condensed electrons, resulting from electron-phonon coupling. They are thus prone to be tuned by lattice strain. NbSe3 is a prototypical example of CDW states, with a chain-like structure displaying two CDWs at 145K and 59K, with wavevectors along and inclined with respect to the chain axis b. Here, we report on the evolution of the lattice structure and CDW properties in the quasi-one-dimensional charge-density-wave system NbSe3 under tensile stresses applied along and perpendicular to the chains axis b by a combination of X-ray diffraction and transport measurements. We find that the lattice structure show exotic Poissons coefficients and strongly anisotropic Youngs moduli while the evolution of the electrical resistance demonstrates shifts of both charge-density-wave critical temperatures that are strongly correlated with the lattice parameters. The two CDW transitions display different behaviours under applied stresses, and suggest that a modification of the band curvature leads to the observed transport signatures.
summary: This work experimentally demonstrates that applying mechanical strain to the CDW material NbSe3 can tune its electronic phase transitions. By combining XRD and transport measurements, the authors establish a strong, quantifiable link between the material's lattice structure and the critical temperatures of the CDW states. This highlights the profound interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic correlations in low-dimensional conductors.
main_problem: The study investigates how applying mechanical lattice strain tunes the Charge Density Wave (CDW) transitions in the quasi-one-dimensional material NbSe3.
main_result: The CDW critical temperatures ($T_{c1}$ and $T_{c2}$) are found to be strongly correlated with the applied lattice strain and resulting lattice parameters, demonstrating a direct coupling between structure and electronic phase transitions.
method: The research combines in-situ X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements under uniaxial tensile stress with electrical transport measurements to probe both structural changes and electronic properties.
model_or_system: The system is NbSe3, a prototypical quasi-one-dimensional conductor exhibiting multiple CDW transitions. The analysis involves relating macroscopic mechanical properties (Young's moduli, Poisson's coefficients) to the electronic susceptibility and CDW critical temperatures.
key_observables: CDW critical temperatures ($T_{c1}, T_{c2}$), lattice parameters ($a, b, c$), electrical resistance $R(T)$, and elastic constants (Young's moduli, Poisson's coefficients).
important_parameters: Applied tensile stresses ($\sigma_b, \sigma_c$), strain ($\epsilon$), and the characteristic temperatures of the two CDW transitions (145 K and 59 K).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes linear elastic behavior and that shear strains are negligible during the deformation process.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of lattice parameters and XRD intensities under applied stresses, and show the temperature dependence of resistance curves ($R(T)$) before and after stress application.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first characterizing the mechanical response of NbSe3 under strain using XRD, then correlating these structural changes with the observed shifts in the CDW transition temperatures derived from transport measurements, and finally discussing the underlying electronic mechanisms.
why_interesting: The strong coupling observed between mechanical strain (a classical/structural input) and the electronic phase transition temperature (CDW) provides a tangible experimental platform for studying emergent quantum phases in correlated materials.
